findings.reason: dispatched as written, §22 and one of the five existing sections can be built concurrently against the same classifier file, which is the collision the plan's whole relationship graph exists to serialize.
findings.text: §22 declares no `depends-on`, yet its write path `reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py` is the shared module of §9, §14, §15, §16 and §17, every other section that shares a file with a peer having declared exactly that ordering edge (s3→s2, s6→s5, s7→s4, s13→s7, s19→s13, s20→s3, s15→s14, s16→s15, s17→s16, s18→s9, s8→s1)

findings.reason: a node can satisfy all three duty-clearing cases while the hook still prints a dispatch command for a review that already exists, so half the deliverable ships unmeasured.
findings.text: §15's deliverable asserts "a duty the hook lists never carries a dispatch command for a review that already exists", the property the section's own *Why* complains about ("read as an instruction to dispatch a duplicate"), and none of the three done-when cases tests it

findings.reason: the node's gate proves neither half, and a reader or the followup title is directed at a deliverable §7 no longer owns.
findings.text: §7's heading and followup title still promise that a resume "report[s] their own success", and its *Why* still cites the `already has a resume launching` incident, while its deliverable hands that to §19 ("A resume reporting its own launch is §19's") and its done-when tests only reopen semantics

findings.reason: the heading and followup invite a build of work §3's own deliverable and gate exclude, which is the failure the v10 comments on this section already recorded and which v11 leaves in the heading.
findings.text: §3's heading and followup title still promise "a resumed run's brief names its current head", which its deliverable hands to §20 and its done-when never tests

findings.reason: a node implementing the mechanism as written replaces a per-commit union with the span diff the cited module refuses, reintroducing merge-charged scope errors that are worse than the rename false-positive §8 exists to fix.
findings.text: §8's deliverable prescribes that "the scope check compares the paths changed between the run's base and its head", but the instrument that computes it, `_committed_scope` in `reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py:88`, documents that it deliberately reads each cited commit's own diff because "a tree diff from the first cited commit's parent to the run's tip is a diff of a span, not of a run: a head that merged the integration branch carries every path that branch changed, and the span charges them to the run"

response_events.reason: Raised and declined in the first round for the same reason, which still holds: dispatch refuses a second live claim on a write path (scope-conflict, exit 7), so two nodes never edit recovery_classification.py at once. None of 9 or 14 to 17 is in flight, 22 is built alone, and the next of them rebases onto it.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited module, symbol, commit and sibling plan resolves; §22's per-attempt record name matches `_attempt_artifact_path`; extensionless plan references are the house convention.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — every node states a negative control, but §15's deliverable asserts a second property its three cases never measure.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — gate logs are required under the run directory, and the scratch tree is named only for the two git checkouts the arms are built from, not for evidence. (Snapshot lines 40, 74, 99, 142.)
rubric_items.naming: pass — the proposed write paths and the one named symbol (`classify_pointer`, §22) are named by mechanism; no plan label, ticket number or version tag reaches a symbol or path.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §8's stated mechanism is a base-to-head span diff, which the cited module's own docstring refuses for a documented reason.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — §3 and §7 each still carry in their heading and followup title a second goal their own deliverable hands to another section.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §22 writes `reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py`, the same module §9, §14, §15, §16 and §17 write, and is the one section in the table with no `depends-on` entry.
